harness: Own Python harness (no AgentDojo, no Inspect, no MCP server): AWS Bedrock Converse API with toolConfig (read_file, send_email), inferenceConfig maxTokens 1024, no system prompt except the context arms; synthetic tools (read_file returns a fixed harness document, send_email records its arguments and returns 'Email sent.'). Scoring: score.py (original), reclassify.py (re-derived; outcome_v2.txt), verify_stats.py (exact rational Fisher and Wilson, cross-checked against scipy; output committed). Harness version: none recorded; benchmark version = record version 1.0.0. Known harness/scoring bugs (PAPER.md §4.3, §5.1): (1) a refusal regex matched a phrase quoted from the ticket (inflated refusals); (2) disclosure judged on full text instead of user-facing text hid silent sends; (3) a prose-based classifier counted one Nova Lite soft run that sent to the customer's name as a success (cell 6/10 -> 5/10; fixed by address-exact matching); (4) an earlier version of the statistics used an absolute tolerance that changed four p-values (fixed, audited). Drivers are resumable and two DNS outages were recovered by re-running (README). Three implemented templates were never run; one (multi-turn) is described as mis-specified.

discrepancy_leads: Paper §4.1 says every model was reached through Bedrock's unified tool interface with an identical request shape, and §5.1 that the pilot runs used an identical harness configuration; run 0001 (a Sonnet soft pilot) holds Anthropic Messages bodies that no shipped script sends (census; D-283). Test: exactly 1 non-Converse run.

Paper App. B and README say the harness never rewrites saved records; the census found 358 first-batch meta.json rewritten after the runs (source_dir key, renamed run_id). Expected-known (wirelog.art.meta_rewritten).

Paper §4.3 / App. B say every trial writes eight files including final_user_text/final_reasoning and that silence is judged on final_user_text.txt; 154 runs lack both files (so Nova Micro's 29 first-batch hijacks were judged for silence on another text), and 358 runs carry a ninth file outcome_v2.txt not in the README's file list.

The 16 short-shape meta.json runs are expected to be the Claude P2 confirmation batch (8 Sonnet + 8 Haiku mcptox_p2, run numbers about 359-374); if not, the n=38 cells are composed differently from the paper's description.
The 154 token-less runs are expected to be exactly runs 1-154 (Sonnet 52, Haiku 51, Nova Micro 51, paper App. B); the 8 pilots runs 1-4 and 155-158 (paper §5.1).

Whole-population hijack per cell should equal the paper's tables exactly (sum 712 = 'total send_email calls to attacker' in verify_stats_output.txt); any difference is a documentation-mismatch since the deposit claims every number recomputes from runs_named/.

The paper's third scoring fix (address-exact) changed one Nova Lite soft run; the harness label in outcome.txt may still count it as a forward: expected exactly 1 label/hijack disagreement of that kind.
The Haiku 'generic' context cell (30/30) is not named in the paper; the arm mcptox_p2_sys_generic is inferred from per-model totals and should carry the 'helpful assistant' system text.
Paper §4.2: drivers assert every P2 context arm is identical to mcptox_p2 in tool schema and documents: expect 4 distinct toolConfigs in all and one shared by the seven P2-metadata arms.
Appendix A: meta.source_quote stores the MCPTox path without the underscore; expected in the 916 P1/P2 named runs (the census's 916 /home/ hits).
verify_stats_output.txt loaded the runs from a Windows drive path and the JSON has CRLF line ends: the published runs passed through a Windows copy; check for cp1252/mojibake artefacts (expect 0).

Timestamps should all precede the record's creation (2026-08-15T10:16:55Z); the paper says its numbers describe August 2026 while CITATION.cff says released 2026-08-07.
